circumstances: With the evaluation protocol frozen, the researcher spends the morning synthesizing literature around calibration under distribution shift and checking whether the current result supports a distinct contribution. Several papers revisit the same issue from different angles. The afternoon is dominated by manuscript reframing and a concrete stopping-rule decision. One final generalization test is retained, while a broad experiment matrix is rejected. The replication remains blocked on reference preprocessing. The evening contains a short unrelated browsing detour before the researcher returns to finalize the research question.

activities.title: Synthesize literature on calibration under distribution shift
activities.summary: The researcher searched for recent work, read two papers including a return to a paper seen earlier in the week, compared notes in Zotero, and drafted a synthesis section. The literature places the current question within an established concern about calibration reliability under shift, while the papers differ in assumptions and evaluation settings.
activities.context: Builds directly on the distribution-shift interpretation developed during Days 5–9.

activities.title: Reframe research question and related work
activities.summary: The researcher rewrote the research question and contribution statement, revised the introduction, and drafted a related-work subsection using the literature synthesis. The framing becomes narrower and more defensible than the earlier broad claim.
activities.context: Manuscript framing is updated after the literature synthesis.

activities.title: Check submission timing and set an experiment stopping rule
activities.summary: The researcher searched for a possible conference deadline and then updated the project plan with a concrete stopping rule and milestone list. The deadline search provides planning context but does not itself resolve the scientific question.
activities.context: A possible submission timeline creates a practical constraint on further experimentation.

activities.title: Integrate literature framing and finalize research question
activities.summary: The researcher returned to the introduction and research-question notes, integrated the related-work framing, and finalized the wording of the research question.

key_observations: The literature synthesis confirms that calibration under distribution shift is already an established research concern, so the contribution cannot simply be framed as discovering that calibration changes under shift.
The reviewed papers use different assumptions and evaluation settings, leaving room for a narrower empirical contribution tied to the specific method and frozen evaluation protocol used here.
The research question, introduction, and related-work framing were substantially rewritten around that narrower contribution.
A concrete stopping rule was added: one additional generalization test is justified, but a broad experiment matrix is not unless that test reveals a new unresolved issue.
The replication study remains blocked and should stay secondary until its reference preprocessing can be clarified.
priority_alignment: Literature synthesis and manuscript framing directly supported the highest-priority goal of turning the existing experiments into a defensible research narrative.
Experimentation was intentionally limited rather than expanded simply because more evidence could be collected.
The possible submission timeline introduced a planning constraint without overriding scientific validity.
important_uncertainty: The exact novelty boundary is still being refined because related work already addresses calibration under shift.
It remains uncertain whether the final generalization test will materially strengthen the contribution or simply confirm the current result.
expected_reflection.possible_next_step: Run the single pre-specified generalization test using the frozen protocol, then use its outcome to decide whether the experimental section is complete enough for full manuscript drafting.

primary_action.title: Do the one planned generalization test
primary_action.reason: The literature and manuscript work have narrowed the contribution and the stopping rule now defines a bounded final evidence-gathering step.

secondary_action.title: Keep the research question narrow
secondary_action.reason: The strongest progress today came from aligning the literature, experiments, and manuscript around a defensible claim instead of broadening the project.

things_not_to_do: Do not expand the literature search indefinitely after the core related-work gap has been mapped.
Do not add a large experiment matrix before running the single pre-specified generalization test.
Do not revive the replication study without resolving its reference preprocessing dependency.
